pattern.crimePattern: cheated trader kills a bale wholesaler who refused a refund and takes his cash
pattern.notes: Fictional godown and traders in a real market. Bale grading and seals shown as common practice; to be checked by the cultural reader.

ob.reportedBy: Lucas Mbithi, business partner, Nyaberi & Mbithi Mitumba, Gikomba
ob.text: Lucas Mbithi reports that his business partner, Hezron Nyaberi (61), mitumba bale wholesaler, was found dead in their godown on the Gikomba riverside lane at 06:10. The leather cash pouch he always wears on his belt is missing.

people.name: Hezron Nyaberi
people.bio: Thirty years in Gikomba. Sells pressed bales of second-hand clothes by grade. Wears a leather cash pouch on his belt day and night.

image.brief: Kenyan man, early 60s, flat cap, worn tweed jacket over a sweater, a brown leather pouch on his belt stamped H.N., hard and amused face, ID-photo framing

people.name: Felistus Wakesho
people.bio: Last week she paid KSh 38,000, borrowed from her chama, for a "first grade" bale that turned out to be rags. Hezron refused a refund.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, mid 40s, kanga tied over her dress as an apron, hair under a knitted cap against the dawn cold, a bale-opening knife on a string at her waist, exhausted and angry, ID-photo framing

people.name: Lucas Mbithi
people.bio: Buys bales off the ships in Mombasa. He and Hezron have been fighting over the split of the profits.

locations.name: Nyaberi & Mbithi Mitumba godown, Gikomba riverside
locations.description: Before dawn. A tin-roofed godown stacked to the beams with pressed bales, each strapped and closed with a numbered plastic seal. One bulb. Outside, handcarts rattle up the slope in the dark.

hotspots.label: Between the bales
hotspots.text: Hezron lies between two bales. An iron lever bar, the kind used to prise bales open, is on the ground. His belt clip is empty.

hotspots.label: On the floor
hotspots.text: A plastic bale seal lies on the concrete, cut open. It doesn't belong to any bale in here.

hotspots.label: Dispatch book on the crate
hotspots.text: Hezron's dispatch book: every bale, its seal number, grade and buyer. Today's page has writing on it.

hotspots.label: Handcart in the lane
hotspots.text: Hamisi Baya has stopped his empty mkokoteni outside and won't come in.

hotspots.label: Grade board
hotspots.text: A chalk board: "1st grade — 2nd grade — 3rd grade — rags". Different prices for each. Most buyers can't see inside a pressed bale before they pay.

image.brief: interior of a tin-roofed mitumba godown at Gikomba market before dawn, pressed bales of second-hand clothes strapped and sealed with numbered plastic tags stacked to the roof, a single bare bulb, an iron lever bar on the concrete floor, a chalk grade board on the wall, no people in focus

locations.name: Stall C-17 (Felistus Wakesho)
locations.description: A wooden stall of children's clothes on hangers. A bale opened yesterday sits at the back, spilling grey rags. A steel stall box with a padlock is chained to the leg of the table.

hotspots.label: Opened bale at the back
hotspots.text: The bale she paid for. On top, a few children's shirts. Underneath, rags.

hotspots.label: Locked stall box
hotspots.text: A steel box, padlocked and chained to the table leg. Her key is on a string round her neck.

facts.text: Lucas Mbithi found his partner Hezron Nyaberi dead in their godown at 06:10.
The leather cash pouch Hezron always wears on his belt is gone.
Hezron was struck with an iron lever bar used for prising bales open.
An opened bale seal, A-2291, lies on the godown floor. No bale in the godown carries that number.
Dispatch book, last Wednesday: 'A-2291 — 1st grade kids — F. Wakesho, C-17 — KSh 38,000 cash.'
Dispatch book, today at 04:40, in Hezron's hand: 'Wakesho came about A-2291. Rags she says. No refund.'
Dispatch book, last month: 'W. Akello — NO MORE BALES. Complained in public.'
Hamisi loaded two bales for Daudi Gichohi at the godown from 04:45 to 04:50.
Hamisi: at 04:50 Hezron was alive, laughing at a woman who was shouting about rags.
Hamisi: about 04:55, pushing up the lane, the same woman hurried past him carrying a brown leather pouch like the one Hezron wears.
At stall C-17, the bale Felistus opened last week: a thin layer of children's shirts over rags.
Felistus's locked stall box holds Hezron's leather pouch, stamped H.N., with KSh 41,000 inside.
Also in the box: a chama loan card, 'F. Wakesho — KSh 38,000'.
Felistus: "He cheated me. I won't pretend he didn't."
Felistus: "This morning I opened at my own stall at five. I never went down to his godown."
Felistus admits she went to the godown at about 04:40 with the seal to beg for a refund. She says he laughed and she left before five.
Lucas: "I was on the overnight bus from Mombasa. I came straight here."
Lucas: Hezron never took that pouch off, not even to sleep.
Lucas: he and Hezron argued about the split. "Sixty-forty. He wanted seventy-thirty. We would have fixed it."
Lucas's ticket: overnight bus Mombasa to Nairobi, departed 22:00, arrived 05:45. He reached the godown at 06:10.
Winnie: "I don't go near his godown since he cut me off. I opened my stall at quarter to five."
Winnie: Felistus lost everything on that bale. "The whole market knew."
Esther: Winnie opened her stall at 04:45 with a crowd of early buyers and never left it.
Daudi: Hamisi delivered his two bales to his stall in the upper market at 05:00. Daudi was waiting there from 04:30.

interrogations.intro: Felistus keeps folding the same small shirt. "Hezron? Dead? God forgive me, I said things about him yesterday."

topics.reply: Many bales have seals. Many numbers.
Thirty-eight thousand. A chama loan. "First grade." I opened it and it was rags. He said sell rags as rags.
Hamisi pushes everyone's bales. He sees everyone. What does he say?

interrogations.intro: Lucas is still holding his backpack. "I got off the bus and came straight here. Straight here."

topics.reply: He never took it off. He slept with it. Whoever did this knew it was there.
We argued about the split. Sixty-forty, seventy-thirty. Business. I was in Mombasa buying his bales.

interrogations.intro: Winnie doesn't stop hanging blouses. "I don't talk about that man."

topics.reply: Felistus lost everything on that bale. The whole market knew. She cried at my stall for an hour.
Ask Mama Esther next door. She watched me sell all morning.

interrogations.intro: Hamisi leans on his cart. "I push bales. Every morning, the same. This morning was not the same."

topics.reply: That is the woman. She was shouting about rags. Then she passed me in the lane, fast, holding a pouch against her chest. I thought, she got her money back.
Two bales for Mzee Daudi, upper market. Call him. I delivered at five.

contradictions.reaction: I went to show him the seal. That is all. I begged him. Thirty-eight thousand, my chama's money. He laughed at me. Then I left. Before five, I swear.

prosecutor.pass: His note puts her there, the porter puts the pouch in her hands, and the warrant puts it in her box. That will hold.
fail: Doesn't hold up. A partner on a bus isn't a partner in the godown. Who was there at ten to five?
No. Follow the seal number, then follow the pouch.

proof.concludes: Felistus said she never went to the godown, but at 04:40 Hezron wrote that she came about A-2291, and her opened seal is on his floor. Pressed, she admits being there.
At 04:50 Hezron was alive and she was still there, shouting. At 04:55 she hurried up the lane holding a pouch like his.
Hezron's own pouch, stamped H.N., is locked in her stall box. Felistus Wakesho killed Hezron.

eliminations.why: Lucas was on the overnight bus until 05:45 and reached the godown at 06:10.
Winnie was serving early buyers at her stall from 04:45, with Esther beside her.
Hamisi left the godown with Daudi's bales at 04:50 and delivered them to the upper market at 05:00.
Daudi was waiting at his own stall in the upper market from 04:30.

reconstruction.text: Last Wednesday. Felistus pays KSh 38,000, a loan from her chama, for bale A-2291, "first grade children's". She opens it at her stall. Rags.
04:40. She comes to the godown with the cut seal in her hand. Hezron writes it in his book and laughs. "Sell rags as rags."
04:50. Hamisi wheels out two bales for another trader. She is still there, shouting.
As soon as the cart is gone, she picks up the lever bar. Then she takes his pouch: "my refund". The seal falls from her hand.
04:55. She passes Hamisi in the lane with the pouch against her chest. By five she is at stall C-17, opening a bale as if she had never left.

tier1.line: Every seal has a number, and Hezron wrote every number down. Match the one on the floor.

tier2.line: He wrote her name at 04:40. The porter saw her with a pouch at 04:55. Now you have grounds.

glossary.def: Second-hand clothes, imported in pressed bales.
Savings group whose members pool money and lend to each other.
Printed cotton cloth, often with a proverb along the edge.
Respectful word for an older man.
Mother; also a respectful way to address or name a woman.

ui.beatNotes: Serial numbers: seals, invoices and receipts with numbers can be dragged onto each other in the notebook; matching numbers snap together with a click. Used constantly from here on.
